erin: quick heads-up — int4 onboarding for LlamaX-3B variant shows a weird wraparound at the head-group boundary, looks like rotary indexing overflow?

sam: can you paste the minimal repro?

erin: repro below — converted model -> int4 using our quant pipeline, running the streaming lm-eval on a small prompt set. noticed token ids > 32768 mapping back to low ids in kvcache.

erin: ```
# convert + eval (what I ran)
python3 tools/convert_quant.py --model LlamaX-3B --quant int4 --out /tmp/lx3b-q4
python3 infra/run_eval.py --model /tmp/lx3b-q4 --prompts data/small_eval.jsonl --stream
```

jia: that sounds like index wrap. which rotary implementation are you using? per-head or multiplexed?

erin: per-head, head_dim=64, rotary_base=10000. suspect the indexmap when splitting heads for the int4 layout forgot to add the head offset, so head 8+ starts reusing earlier rows.

mike: screenshot of a kv dump? a quick hexdump of a few token ids around the boundary would help.

erin: pasted small dump, token ids on input sequence: [32000, 32001, 32002, 0, 1, 2] — expected continuous but rotation cos/sin show sudden phase reset at 32002->0.

erin: snippet: ```
# kvcache indices observed
layer3.head8.kv_idx: [31996,31997,31998,31999,0,1,2]
```

alicia: ugh that explains the burst of hallucinations we saw in the evals (ppl jump ~12->23). did you compare fp16 baseline?

erin: yes fp16 baseline ppl ~11.8, int4 naive ppl ~22.9. int4 with per-head index fix (local patch) ppl ~12.4 on same prompts.

sam: nice. what's the patch? is it in conversion or runtime remap?

erin: quick diff: when computing head_offset in convert_quant, we were doing `head_offset = head * head_dim` but then modulo by vocab_stride accidentally; changed to `head_offset = head * head_dim + head_group * head_group_stride` to match layout. tiny one-liner.

triage-bot: New commit pushed to branch `fix/int4-head-offsets` by erin — CI queued. :white_check_mark:

jia: can you run a short ablation: int4 quant, with/without rotary scaling tweaks (scale 1.0 vs 1.12), because we saw scaling interacts badly with wraparound sometimes.

erin: running now. command: `infra/run_eval.py --model /tmp/lx3b-q4-fixed --prompts data/small_eval.jsonl --rotary-scale 1.0,1.12 --metrics ppl,exactmatch`

mike: also check tokenizers — any byteorder or mapping difference? earlier qwen imports had a sentinel mapping that caused +1 shift.

erin: tokenizer checked — identical mapping to fp16 baseline. no extra sentinels.

alicia: do we need to propagate fix to the runtime shim too? might hit Dedicated customers that hot-swap int4 model variants.

erin: yes planning to patch both convert and runtime. runtime already has a head-map table, but the converter output didn't align with it. will add validation that verifies monotonicity of kv indices per layer.

sam: make a small unit test for the converter: generate synthetic head groups and assert `sorted(unique(kv_idx)) == list(range(start, start+N))` — fail early.

erin: will add test. leaving notes in PR describing how this caused our eval regression and linking the ppl numbers.

jia: after you push, can we run the full long-context regressions? last time wraparound only appeared beyond 2k tokens.

erin: queued longctx run on a 10k token synthetic story set, ETA ~2h. I'll post results in this thread.

mike: thanks — great catch. weird that per-head packing only fails in our int4 layout. implies our int4 packing stride math needs a docstring. :sweat_smile:

erin: agreed — adding a short design note to `docs/quant_layouts.md` about head_group vs head_stride mapping and compatibility matrix for Llama/Mistral/Gemma/Qwen.

triage-bot: Long-run eval job `LR-5873` started (10k tokens, 200 prompts) — logs: https://ci.internal/logs/LR-5873

erin: thanks everyone — will follow up with numbers and a tiny blurb for ops so they can patch runtime if needed. :thumbsup:
